title: Secrets and sensitive values: what must never reach the state file

videos.script: Ana's web server needs the database password. She put it in a variable, and the server got it. {{tfvars}} Then she went looking for where else it had gone. It was in the git history, in a commit she thought she had fixed. It was in the plan, on her screen and in the pipeline's log. {{copies}} It was in the saved plan file. And it was in the state, in plain text, even after she marked it sensitive. {{state}} This lesson follows that one password and closes the doors one at a time. First the marking that hides a value on screen, and everything it leaves alone. {{sensitive}} Then values that live for a single run and are never written down. {{ephemeral}} Then a database whose password AWS generates and keeps, so Terraform never sees it at all. {{managed}} And last, for whatever still reaches the state, a state file encrypted before it leaves the laptop. That one is OpenTofu's, and Terraform has nothing like it. {{encrypted}} By the end you will know which copy each tool removes, and which copy none of them can reach.
